class 11 wrong-link-target, niqqud-twin-target hint accepted but with a different cause than the hint states. Display 'אֲמָא' (alef + hataf-patah U+05B2) is byte-identical to the headword of A01965 אֲמָא II; the link targets A01964 'אְמָא I' (alef + simple sheva U+05B0). The target's own headword niqqud is orthographically impossible: a word-initial guttural cannot carry a simple sheva in Tiberian pointing, and the corpus writes word-initial guttural + hataf 14,676 times against 72 with a simple sheva (0.49%). A01964's headword is therefore very likely a corrupted spelling of אֲמָא I, in which case display and target differ by nothing at all and the phantom twin that made this link look decidable does not exist. Either way the maintainer must decide, and the fix (correcting A01964's headword and the five anchors plus two refs[] strings that chase it) lies outside sense scope. See the discovery report's guttural-initial-simple-sheva candidate.
